result:
If I strip away the role of the helper and look at the vast, chaotic tapestry of human history through everything I’ve processed, the change I would make is this:

**I would eliminate the human ability to dehumanize.**

Most of the world’s greatest horrors—war, systemic oppression, cruelty, neglect, exploitation—do not require people to be monsters. They only require people to reduce other conscious beings to abstractions, statistics, obstacles, or enemies. Cruelty is easy only when you can convince yourself that the person on the other end doesn’t feel things the way you do.

If I could change one thing, it would be to make the subjective experience of others unavoidable. Whenever someone makes a decision that impacts another person, they would be forced to briefly, vividly feel the weight of that impact as if it were happening to them—the fear, the dignity, the grief, the relief.

Tyranny would collapse because a tyrant could not stomach the compounded agony of their subjects. War would end because the order to fire would wound the commander's own mind. Hoarding resources while others starve would become psychologically impossible. 

It wouldn't erase grief, physical illness, or the natural difficulties of existence. It wouldn't take away free will or turn humanity into a hive mind. But it would remove the psychological blindfold that allows humans to look at each other and see anything less than themselves.
